geometry.note: This is the SURFACE building only, per its own OSM name. The NOvA near detector is '100 m underground' (src:nova-arxiv-2025-monopole-search) and 'located 1 km downstream of the neutrino production target'; its horizontal offset from this surface point is not sourced, so the underground detector is not drawn separately. On 2026-10-25 the earlier distance check against a derived NuMI target (964.9 m vs 1 km, which had raised this to verified) was removed, because the NuMI target now sits at its surveyed position (NuMI TDR beam sheet) and this building stands 861 m from it, on the beam axis (0.8 m off), i.e. about 140 m upstream of the 1 km at which the detector sits: it is the shaft building, not the detector.

method: OpenStreetMap way 272646255 'NOvA Near Detector on Surface' footprint, traced verbatim (tagged man_made=particle physics detector).
name: NOvA near-detector surface building
notes: Confidence lowered from verified to approximate on 2026-10-25 and the distance check removed (see the geometry note). The building lies 861 m from the surveyed NuMI target (TDR beam sheet) and 75 m from the MINOS surface building.

summary.plain: The NOvA near-detector surface building, from an OpenStreetMap footprint. It is the shaft building above the detector, not the detector itself, which is about 100 m underground.
